scenes.tts: Tension pays for area. But how does force reach the channel? Through lipid, through a protein tether, or both?
scenes.visual: Title card: Lipid, Tether and People. A channel in a membrane with two arrows arriving: one through the lipid labelled 'membrane tension', one through a protein chain from inside labelled 'possible direct tether force'.
scenes.narration: Tension pays for area. But how does force reach the channel? Through lipid, through a protein tether, or both?

scenes.tts: The idea is the work done by membrane tension. A tether could change that tension, or pull on the channel directly. That would add its own work term.
scenes.visual: The equation ΔG = ΔG₀ − T × ΔA sits in a box labelled membrane-tension work. Beside it, a dashed box labelled direct tether force: an extra term, force times distance?
scenes.narration: The idea is the work done by membrane tension. A tether could change that tension, or pull on the channel directly. That would add its own work term.

scenes.tts: The lipid route has a clean test. Take everything else away.
scenes.visual: Cell components fade away one by one, leaving a single channel.
scenes.narration: The lipid route has a clean test. Take everything else away.

scenes.tts: Purified mouse Pee-AY-zo one was placed in droplet bilayers, with no other cellular components.
scenes.caption: Purified mouse Piezo1 was placed in droplet bilayers, with no other cellular components.
scenes.visual: Two lipid-coated droplets touch; a bilayer forms where they meet, with one channel in it.
scenes.narration: Purified mouse Piezo1 was placed in droplet bilayers, with no other cellular components.

scenes.tts: A droplet bilayer forms where two lipid-coated droplets touch. Nothing from a cell is present.
scenes.visual: Label on the bilayer: droplet bilayer, no cell.
scenes.narration: A droplet bilayer forms where two lipid-coated droplets touch. Nothing from a cell is present.

scenes.tts: Suppose a tether were strictly required for opening. What should the purified channel have done? And what would its opening tell you about a cell?
scenes.visual: On screen: if a tether were required, what should the purified channel do here?
scenes.narration: Suppose a tether were strictly required for opening. What should the purified channel have done? And what would its opening tell you about a cell?

scenes.tts: It should have stayed silent. Yet force still activated it, so protein plus lipid is sufficient there.
scenes.visual: A current trace appears from the droplet bilayer when it is stretched. Label: sufficient in this preparation.
scenes.narration: It should have stayed silent. Yet force still activated it, so protein plus lipid is sufficient there.

scenes.tts: But that says nothing about whether an intact cell also uses a second route.
scenes.visual: A whole cell appears beside the droplet, with a question mark over a second route.
scenes.narration: But that says nothing about whether an intact cell also uses a second route.

scenes.tts: A second route has been proposed. Wang and colleagues described a chain of cadherin, beta-catenin and actin.
scenes.visual: Inside a cultured cell: a chain drawn from the channel through E-cadherin and beta-catenin to actin filaments. Label: Wang and colleagues, 2022.
scenes.narration: A second route has been proposed. Wang and colleagues described a chain of cadherin, beta-catenin and actin.

scenes.tts: Disrupting the channel's link to E cadherin prevented cytoskeleton-dependent gating in their cultured cells.
scenes.caption: Disrupting the channel's link to E-cadherin prevented cytoskeleton-dependent gating in their cultured cells.
scenes.visual: The chain is cut at the E-cadherin link; the cytoskeleton-driven current disappears. Tag: cultured cells.
scenes.narration: Disrupting the channel's link to E-cadherin prevented cytoskeleton-dependent gating in their cultured cells.

scenes.tts: These need not be rivals. Sufficiency in one preparation cannot exclude a route in another. That is why the field has not chosen.
scenes.visual: A two-column table: bilayer shows sufficiency; cultured cells show a coupling route. An equals sign between them, not a versus.
scenes.narration: These need not be rivals. Sufficiency in one preparation cannot exclude a route in another. That is why the field has not chosen.

scenes.tts: There is even a hint that the bilayer misses something. The purified channel lacked the rapid inactivation seen in whole cells.
scenes.visual: Two traces: whole-cell current decays quickly; the bilayer current does not.
scenes.narration: There is even a hint that the bilayer misses something. The purified channel lacked the rapid inactivation seen in whole cells.

scenes.tts: Inactivation is where human genetics meets this biophysics. Distal arthrogryposis is an inherited condition. Joints of the hands and feet are fixed in bent positions from birth.
scenes.visual: A hand and foot schematic with flexed joints. Label: distal arthrogryposis.
scenes.narration: Inactivation is where human genetics meets this biophysics. Distal arthrogryposis is an inherited condition. Joints of the hands and feet are fixed in bent positions from birth.

scenes.tts: Two Pee-AY-zo two variants from such families were tested in a human cell line. Both sped recovery from inactivation. Only one slowed inactivation during the pulse.
scenes.caption: Two Piezo2 variants from such families were tested in a human cell line. Both sped recovery from inactivation. Only one slowed inactivation during the pulse.
scenes.visual: Two variant traces, I802F and E2727del, against wild type. Both recover faster; only E2727del decays more slowly during the pulse. Labels held on screen.
scenes.narration: Two Piezo2 variants from such families were tested in a human cell line. Both sped recovery from inactivation. Only one slowed inactivation during the pulse.

scenes.tts: So slower inactivation is not a rule for every variant. Read each one.
scenes.visual: A crossed-out label: gain of function always means slower inactivation.
scenes.narration: So slower inactivation is not a rule for every variant. Read each one.

scenes.tts: Loss of function looks different in mice and in people. Adult mice lacking Pee-AY-zo two in sensory neurons and Merkel cells lose almost all light-touch behaviour.
scenes.caption: Loss of function looks different in mice and in people. Adult mice lacking Piezo2 in sensory neurons and Merkel cells lose almost all light-touch behaviour.
scenes.visual: Left panel, mouse: Piezo2 deleted in sensory neurons and Merkel cells; light-touch assays nearly flat.
scenes.narration: Loss of function looks different in mice and in people. Adult mice lacking Piezo2 in sensory neurons and Merkel cells lose almost all light-touch behaviour.

scenes.tts: Two people without working Pee-AY-zo two had impaired discriminative touch. Their sense of limb position was profoundly impaired, and worse without vision.
scenes.caption: Two people without working Piezo2 had impaired discriminative touch. Their sense of limb position was profoundly impaired, and worse without vision.
scenes.visual: Right panel, people: two figures; discriminative touch impaired; limb-position errors grow when the eyes are covered.
scenes.narration: Two people without working Piezo2 had impaired discriminative touch. Their sense of limb position was profoundly impaired, and worse without vision.

scenes.tts: But they kept other abilities. Their deficits were selective. Keep the mouse sentences and the human sentences apart.
scenes.visual: The two panels separate, each with its own label: mouse, almost complete light-touch deficit; human, selective deficits.
scenes.narration: But they kept other abilities. Their deficits were selective. Keep the mouse sentences and the human sentences apart.

scenes.tts: Now back to the first question. Why does one channel need one hundred and fourteen helices? In the leading model, still debated, to collect area.
scenes.caption: Now back to the first question. Why does one channel need 114 helices? In the leading model, still debated, to collect area.
scenes.visual: The 114-helix trimer returns, flattening as its projected-area ring widens. Tag: leading model, still debated.
scenes.narration: Now back to the first question. Why does one channel need 114 helices? In the leading model, still debated, to collect area.

scenes.tts: Tension pays for area. Whether a tether adds its own force is a separate question.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Tension pays for area. Whether a tether adds its own force is a separate question.
scenes.narration: Tension pays for area. Whether a tether adds its own force is a separate question.
